changes.balance: Flat price trades the war premium against intact flows; the physical seller (Aramco) is discounting for volume while the headlines escalate. The premium keeps leaking but the floor stays firm without a diplomatic breakthrough.
changes.body: Overnight tape flat-to-soft: WTI ~$89.33 (-0.1% vs Monday's $89.43 settle), Brent Dec ~$100.28 (-4c) at 0003 GMT (Reuters), firming to $100.70 by the Singapore morning (Bloomberg). Brent-WTI holding around $11. New bearish information: Saudi Aramco cut its Arab Light official selling price for Asian buyers to a six-year low (Bloomberg) - a market-share push that reads as a soft demand view. Middle East crude exports exceeded pre-war levels on four days during the last week of September (Reuters, citing Monday shipping data); Kuwait is pumping ~75% of pre-war and Iraq is hiring additional vessels for Hormuz loadings (Bloomberg).
changes.conditional: Diplomatic breakthrough -> premium bleeds further; confirmed strike on Saudi energy infrastructure -> premium rebuilds fast.
changes.delta: WTI ~$89.33 overnight; Brent ~$100.28; Aramco OSP cut to 6-yr low; Gulf exports beat pre-war 4 days last week
changes.title: Tape flat as Aramco discounts and Gulf exports beat pre-war

changes.balance: The release is the ceiling on the product market; the physical drivers (Russia's diesel export ban through Oct 31, China's October product-export halt) are the floor. The first 20 days of front-loaded diesel run straight into the Russian ban's Oct 31 expiry.
changes.body: NYMEX diesel crack settled $101.47 on Monday Oct 5 - back above $100 after Friday's $97.94 close ended eighteen straight above (validated against the refreshed crack history; all-time max $117.92, Sep 16; 3-2-1 at $65.10 vs $75.31 max Aug 28). The overnight session print has the diesel crack at ~$98.97 (Yahoo front-month bar ~02:00 MDT - provisional, not a close). ING's gasoil mark ($85->$70) and the G7's front-loaded diesel are the ceiling; Russia's export ban through Oct 31, China's October halt, and Ukrainian refinery strikes are the floor.
changes.conditional: Front-loaded diesel arrives on schedule -> cracks stay soft into winter; delivery slippage or fresh escalation -> physical tightness reasserts.
changes.delta: Diesel crack $101.47 Monday close (>$100); overnight ~$98.97 provisional
changes.source: Validated crack history (Yahoo front-month futures), refreshed Oct 6, 2026
changes.title: Diesel crack reclaims $100 on Monday's close

changes.balance: September's >$20 WCS blowout (widest since Dec 2023) was a refinery-outage event, not an egress event - and it is already unwinding on restarts. The Nov-Dec egress crunch now trades on the ~Oct 19 apportionment notice, not on refinery demand.
changes.body: The PADD 2 demand snap-back is ~700 kb/d and corroborated two ways: ExxonMobil Joliet restarted ~Sep 28-Oct 2 (QCIntel Sep 28; Price Group Sep 29) and BP Whiting 'returned to normal operations after planned maintenance' (Reuters Sep 21), running at full strength. Corrections carried: the Whiting lockout of ~800 USW members continues but is a labor dispute, not a demand outage; one conflict to watch - Reuters Sep 16 trade sources had Whiting unit overhauls 'until early November' vs the Oct 2 full-strength read, and tomorrow's EIA PADD 2 print arbitrates. Supply healing: Syncrude's ~50-day Mildred Lake coker turnaround wraps ~Oct 5-16 (completion unconfirmed); CNRL's 35-day Horizon upgrader turnaround implies ~Oct 12-13; Suncor Edmonton/Base fall turnarounds roll off mid-month. All AESO-monitored SAGD cogen units at full MC (01:39 MDT).
changes.conditional: EIA PADD 2 prints high-90s -> snap-back confirmed, Sep blowout framed as outage event; prints soft -> Whiting conflict reopens.
changes.delta: ~700 kb/d PADD 2 demand back (Joliet + Whiting); Syncrude TAR wraps ~Oct 5-16 unconfirmed
changes.source: Reuters Sep 21; QCIntel/PriceGroup Sep 28-29; in-house maintenance forecast refreshed Oct 5; AESO CSD Oct 6
changes.title: PADD 2 demand snaps back; September WCS blowout unwinding

changes.balance: The Yemen theater is heating on the ground even as the strait stays quiet. Ships struck near-daily last week, barrels flowing at or above pre-war on the good days, diplomacy stalled, carriers en route.
changes.body: UKMTO disclosed five Hormuz incidents Monday Oct 5: three time-late attacks (LPG tanker 1716 UTC Oct 4; crude tanker 1907 UTC Oct 4; crude tanker above waterline Oct 3), a fresh Monday 1637 UTC strike with engine-room fire, and an IRGC hail ordering an inbound tanker to turn back (complied). TradeWinds counts 11 ships hit in a week (10 tankers + 1 LPG carrier since Sep 29). Red Sea: tanker explosions ~60nm south of Mokha near Bab el-Mandeb Oct 5. Ukraine overnight Oct 5-6: 650-drone attack on Moscow region hit the Volodarsk oil depot (Transneft, ~3 Mt/yr, Moscow's largest) with visible fire. The Houthis claimed Monday attacks on Riyadh airport, Rabigh refinery, and Abha (no Saudi confirmation); Saudi-backed forces seized Mocha. Ceasefire: stalemate. US buildup timeline stands.
changes.conditional: Confirmed strike on Saudi energy infrastructure -> premium rebuilds; ceasefire proposal advances -> premium bleeds.
changes.delta: UKMTO: 5 incidents Monday (fresh engine-room-fire strike); TradeWinds: 11 ships in a week; Ukraine 650-drone attack hits Volodarsk depot
changes.source: UKMTO via gCaptain/BOE Report; TradeWinds; Reuters; Bloomberg, Oct 5-6, 2026

Cenovus to acquire Athabasca Oil for C$5.7B; Ithaca buys Suncor offshore
changes.delta: Cenovus-Athabasca C$5.7B EV (Oct 5); Ithaca-Suncor US$860M + US$250M contingent (Oct 5)
changes.body: Cenovus agreed to acquire Athabasca Oil Corporation for an implied C$5.7B enterprise value (announced Oct 5): ~45,000 boe/d near Christina Lake/Foster Creek, path to 115,000 bbl/d thermal by 2032, ~C$85M/yr synergies, close expected December 2026. Follows the C$8.6B MEG Energy acquisition (closed Nov 2025) - Cenovus is consolidating the Christina Lake/Foster Creek fairway. Separately, Ithaca Energy (UK) is buying Suncor's East Coast offshore assets (Terra Nova, White Rose, West White Rose) for US$860M cash plus up to US$250M contingent (announced Oct 5). Both are M&A with no WCSB maintenance implication, but the Cenovus deal is a thermal-growth accelerant into 2027-32.
changes.balance: Consolidation into well-funded SAGD operators accelerates thermal growth; watch forward supply (OSM expects record 1.85 MMbpd thermal in Q4 2026).
changes.conditional: Deal closes December -> Cenovus thermal machine absorbs Leismer/Corner growth; blocked -> Athabasca standalone.
changes.source: GlobeNewswire via CRWEWorld; Dow Jones via Morningstar; OEDigital
